evidence.quote: Range lights were placed at the entrance to St. Peters Bay on the northern shore of Prince Edward Island in 1868.

After Parliament made an appropriation of $1,600 for range towers at the entrance of St. Peters Harbour, tenders were invited for their construction, and a contract for the sum of $550 was awarded to James Barclay of Ellerslie.
The towers were completed in 1878 at a total cost of $1,031.12.

notes_for_editor: Thin documentary base: mostly secondary sources (Lighthouse Friends, society pages). Dates of the present tower (1878 vs 1881 vs 1876?) conflict; the record's tower may be the front range light moved several times. Lighthouse Friends calls Drake 'last keeper' while the keeper list ends 1963; the 1965 two skeleton ranges are as reported there. Keeper table 1902 entry matched by column position in OCR. Pre-1900 reports are not in the corpus; the 1888 and 1896 facts are as quoted by Lighthouse Friends, not read directly. No newspapers searched.
